cases.query: What changed in zod from 3.23.8 to 4.0.0?

breaking.change: Error customization: drops invalid_type_error and required_error
breaking.quote: The invalid_type_error / required_error params have been dropped.

breaking.change: Error customization: drops errorMap
breaking.quote: This is renamed to error.

breaking.change: ZodError: changes to .message
breaking.quote: Previously the .message property on ZodError was a JSON.stringified copy of the .issues array.

breaking.change: ZodError: updates issue formats
breaking.quote: The issue formats have been dramatically streamlined.

breaking.change: ZodError: changes error map precedence
breaking.quote: The error map precedence has been changed to be more consistent.

breaking.change: ZodError: drops .formErrors
breaking.quote: This API was identical to .flatten(). It exists for historical reasons and isn't documented.

breaking.change: ZodError: drops .errors
breaking.quote: This API was an alias for .issues in Zod v3 but has been removed.

breaking.change: z.number(): no infinite values
breaking.quote: POSITIVE_INFINITY and NEGATIVE_INFINITY are no longer considered valid values for z.number().

breaking.change: z.number(): .safe() no longer accepts floats
breaking.quote: In Zod 3, z.number().safe() is deprecated. It now behaves identically to .int() (see below).

breaking.change: z.number(): .int() accepts safe integers only
breaking.quote: The z.number().int() API no longer accepts unsafe integers (outside the range of Number.MIN_SAFE_INTEGER and Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER).

breaking.change: z.string() updates: stricter .uuid()
breaking.quote: The z.uuid() now validates UUIDs more strictly against the RFC 9562/4122 specification; specifically, the variant bits must be 10 per the spec.

breaking.change: z.string() updates: no padding in .base64url()
breaking.quote: Padding is no longer allowed in z.base64url() (formerly z.string().base64url()).

breaking.change: z.string() updates: drops z.string().ip()
breaking.quote: This has been replaced with separate .ipv4() and .ipv6() methods.

breaking.change: z.string() updates: updates z.string().ipv6()
breaking.quote: Validation now happens using the new URL() constructor, which is far more robust than the old regular expression approach.

breaking.change: z.string() updates: drops z.string().cidr()
breaking.quote: Similarly, this has been replaced with separate .cidrv4() and .cidrv6() methods.

breaking.change: z.object(): defaults applied within optional fields
breaking.quote: Defaults inside your properties are applied, even within optional fields.

breaking.change: z.object(): drops .nonstrict()
breaking.quote: This long-deprecated alias for .strip() has been removed.

breaking.change: z.object(): drops .deepPartial()
breaking.quote: This has been long deprecated in Zod 3 and it now removed in Zod 4.

breaking.change: z.object(): changes z.unknown() optionality
breaking.quote: The z.unknown() and z.any() types are no longer marked as "key optional" in the inferred types.

breaking.change: z.array(): changes .nonempty() type
breaking.quote: This now behaves identically to z.array().min(1).

breaking.change: .refine(): ignores type predicates
breaking.quote: In Zod 3, passing a type predicate as a refinement functions could still narrow the type of a schema. This wasn't documented but was discussed in some issues. This is no longer the case.

breaking.change: .refine(): drops ctx.path
breaking.quote: Zod's new parsing architecture does not eagerly evaluate the path array.

breaking.change: .refine(): drops function as second argument
breaking.quote: The following horrifying overload has been removed.

breaking.change: z.ostring(), etc dropped
breaking.quote: The undocumented convenience methods z.ostring(), z.onumber(), etc. have been removed.

breaking.change: z.literal(): drops symbol support
breaking.quote: Symbols aren't considered literal values, nor can they be simply compared with ===.

breaking.change: static .create() factories dropped
breaking.quote: Previously all Zod classes defined a static .create() method. These are now implemented as standalone factory functions.

breaking.change: z.record(): drops single argument usage
breaking.quote: Before, z.record() could be used with a single argument. This is no longer supported.

breaking.change: z.intersection(): throws Error on merge conflict
breaking.quote: In Zod 4, this will throw a regular Error instead.

breaking.change: z.coerce input type is unknown
breaking.quote: The input type of all z.coerce schemas is now unknown.

breaking.change: .default() short-circuits on undefined and applies to the output type
breaking.quote: If the input is undefined, ZodDefault short-circuits the parsing process and returns the default value.

breaking.change: z.function() is no longer a Zod schema
breaking.quote: The result of z.function() is no longer a Zod schema.

breaking.change: z.record() with an enum key schema is exhaustive
breaking.quote: In Zod 3, passing an enum into z.record() as a key schema would result in a partial type

breaking.change: app.del() was removed
breaking.quote: Express 5 no longer supports the app.del() function.

breaking.change: app.param(fn) was removed
breaking.quote: The app.param(fn) signature was used for modifying the behavior of the app.param(name, fn) function. It has been deprecated since v4.11.0, and Express 5 no longer supports it at all.

breaking.change: Pluralized method names: req.acceptsCharset, acceptsEncoding, acceptsLanguage were removed
breaking.quote: The following method names have been pluralized.

breaking.change: A leading colon in app.param(name, fn) is no longer stripped
breaking.quote: Leading colon (:) in the name for app.param(name, fn)

breaking.change: req.param(name) was removed
breaking.quote: This potentially confusing and dangerous method of retrieving form data has been removed.

breaking.change: res.json(obj, status) was removed
breaking.quote: Express 5 no longer supports the signature res.json(obj, status).

breaking.change: res.jsonp(obj, status) was removed
breaking.quote: Express 5 no longer supports the signature res.jsonp(obj, status).

breaking.change: res.redirect(url, status) was removed
breaking.quote: Express 5 no longer supports the signature res.redirect(url, status).

breaking.change: The magic 'back' value of res.redirect and res.location was removed
breaking.quote: Express 5 no longer supports the magic string back in the res.redirect() and res.location() methods.

breaking.change: res.send(body, status) was removed
breaking.quote: Express 5 no longer supports the signature res.send(obj, status).

breaking.change: res.send(status) with a number was removed
breaking.quote: Express 5 no longer supports the signature res.send(status), where status is a number.

breaking.change: res.sendfile() was removed
breaking.quote: The res.sendfile() function has been replaced by a camel-cased version res.sendFile() in Express 5.

breaking.change: res.sendFile() options changed
breaking.quote: The hidden and from options for res.sendFile() are no longer supported.

breaking.change: express.static() options changed
breaking.quote: The hidden and from options for express.static() are no longer supported.

breaking.change: router.param(fn) was removed
breaking.quote: The router.param(fn) signature was used for modifying the behavior of the router.param(name, fn) function. It has been deprecated since v4.11.0, and Express 5 no longer supports it at all.

breaking.change: express.static.mime was removed
breaking.quote: In Express 5, mime is no longer an exported property of the static field.

breaking.change: MIME types changed
breaking.quote: Several MIME types have changed due to updates in mime-db. These changes only affect express.static() and res.sendFile().

breaking.change: The express:router debug logs changed
breaking.quote: Router handling logic is now performed by a separate dependency (router) maintained by the Express team, so debug logs have moved to a different namespace.

breaking.change: Path route matching syntax changed (path-to-regexp 8)
breaking.quote: The following changes have been made to how the path string is matched to an incoming request:

breaking.change: Rejected promises from middleware and handlers are handled as errors
breaking.quote: Request middleware and handlers that return rejected promises are now handled by forwarding the rejected value as an Error to the error handling middleware.

breaking.change: express.urlencoded defaults extended to false
breaking.quote: The express.urlencoded method makes the extended option false by default.

breaking.change: express.static no longer serves dotfiles by default
breaking.quote: The express.static middleware's dotfiles option now defaults to "ignore".

breaking.change: router.param() no longer accepts an array of names
breaking.quote: router.param(name, fn) no longer accepts an array for name.

breaking.change: app.listen behaviour changed
breaking.quote: In Express 5, the app.listen method will invoke the user-provided callback function (if provided) when the server receives an error event.

breaking.change: app.router was removed
breaking.quote: The app.router object, which was removed in Express 4, has made a comeback in Express 5.

breaking.change: req.body is undefined when the body has not been parsed
breaking.quote: The req.body property returns undefined when the body has not been parsed. In Express 4, it returns {} by default.

breaking.change: req.host keeps the port
breaking.quote: In Express 4, the req.host function incorrectly stripped off the port number if it was present. In Express 5, the port number is maintained.

breaking.change: req.params changed
breaking.quote: The req.params object now has a null prototype when using string paths.

breaking.change: req.query is a getter and its parser changed
breaking.quote: The req.query property is no longer a writable property and is instead a getter.

breaking.change: res.clearCookie ignores maxAge and expires
breaking.quote: The res.clearCookie method ignores the maxAge and expires options provided by the user.

breaking.change: res.status only accepts integers 100-999
breaking.quote: The res.status method only accepts integers in the range of 100 to 999, following the behavior defined by Node.js, and it returns an error when the status code is not an integer.

breaking.change: res.vary throws without a field argument
breaking.quote: The res.vary throws an error when the field argument is missing.

breaking.change: Node.js 18 or newer is required
breaking.quote: Dropped support for Node.js versions before v18.
